newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Rwanda genocide tribunal rejects defence motion.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda genocide tribunal rejects defence motion.

text.p: The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda rejected on Thursday a defence motion saying it had no authority to try suspected leaders of Rwanda's genocide in 1994.

It rejected the motion from lawyer Evans Monari defending Joseph Kanyabashi that the tribunal, set up by the U.N. Security Council in 1994, had no authority because it was not established by the U.N. General Assembly or an international treaty.
In a 13-page decision, the trial chamber of the tribunal said Kanyabashi's defence should have submitted the preliminary motion within 60 days of the initial appearance of the accused.
The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda was modelled on the Hague-based criminal tribunal for the former Yugoslavia which was set up by the United Nations in 1993.
The tribunal for the former Yugoslavia was the first international body for the prosecution of war crimes since the Nuremberg and Tokyo trials following World War Two.
The Rwanda tribunal based in northern Tanzania has been plagued by problems in bringing to justice the leaders of the 1994 genocide in Rwanda of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
